headline: Heretic Enters the Archive
lede: Heretic’s creator is stepping away and freezing the repository in its present form. No successor is named; its future now belongs to contributors who choose to organize around it.

headline: Linux Boots Inside WebAssembly
lede: A real Linux kernel, an AArch64 user space, and a Debian-like environment now run in a browser tab. Unkernel assembles the stack from Linux-WASM, Emscripten, Mesa, Wayland, and persistent browser storage.

headline: One Loom Weaves, Knits, and Braids
lede: Cornell’s Kneadix combines three textile techniques in one programmable machine. Rotating gears, adjustable combs, and tension sensors produce fabrics with curved edges, mixed stretch, and room for embedded wiring.

headline: DeepCrossAttention Reaches Three Times Faster
lede: Google Research replaces fixed residual addition with token-specific retrieval across transformer depth. The architecture reports comparable quality with fewer parameters, training steps, and—under some tests—up to three times the speed.

headline: Knuth Closes the Error Inbox
lede: Donald Knuth is pausing new reports of errors in his books after AI-assisted submissions overwhelmed his ability to verify them. The notice is a small, precise record of a larger problem: machines can multiply careful work faster than a human can review it.

headline: How Balatro Became Balatro
lede: LocalThunk traces the game from a private Lua prototype in 2021 to its 2024 release across platforms. The timeline records the additions, playtesting, sudden visibility, and personal cost behind an unlikely commercial success.

headline: An AI Finds a Name in the Archive
lede: GPT-6.2 Astra linked an anonymous 1808 sketchbook at Yale to Louis-Guy-Charles-Guillaume de Chabot by connecting images, itineraries, handwriting, and a scarcely indexed diary. The attribution remains a case study in machine-assisted scholarship: useful, persistent, and dependent on human verification.

headline: Arcosanti Still Tests the City
lede: Paolo Soleri’s unfinished Arizona arcology remains a vivid argument for dense, communal, resource-conscious living. Its tiny population and incomplete plan make it less a finished model than a durable test of what architecture can—and cannot—solve.
pullquote: A city is more than its architecture; it is the conditions that let people stay.

headline: WebRTC Skimmers Reached Five Retailers
lede: Payment-skimming code was found on five major shopping sites before Black Friday. The scripts targeted mobile checkout pages and sent test card data outward through Cloudflare-relayed WebRTC channels; the sites have since removed them.

headline: A Classroom Kit Puts Transmutation to Test
lede: A proposed kit aims to reproduce disputed underwater electrical-discharge experiments that reportedly produced new elements. Before anyone sells the apparatus, its designers want independent laboratory replication, tighter controls, and a safer path through the extraordinary claims.
